facts.fact: Lesotho is named among 25 African countries where Starlink operates as of November 2025, with Vodacom authorised to resell Starlink equipment and broadband services in its markets.
Starlink officially launched in Maseru on Monday 30 June 2025 through exclusive reseller T-Connect Lesotho, at M10 per access session with hotspots planned in all 10 districts.
Starlink operates in Lesotho under a 10-year licence (grant date not given; date is the article's publication date), with opposition over foreign ownership and a fast-tracking allegation.
The Lesotho Communications Authority granted Starlink a 10-year operating licence on 14 April 2025 after a year-long regulatory review.
Starlink became available in Lesotho at a launch by authorised reseller T-Connect Lesotho in Maseru, with business packages from M1,600 a month and M10 hotspot access for uncapped daily data.

The Lesotho Communications Authority granted Starlink a 10-year licence, Lesotho's first satellite internet licence, to serve individuals and businesses; no grant date is given, so the article date is used.

Starlink's Network Services Licence application (10-year term if approved) was pending before the LCA, in public consultation with comments closing 20 March 2025, and opposed by Section 2 over 100% foreign ownership.
